title: 29 CFR 1910.331 — Scope
jurisdiction_scope: US federal general industry; applicability depends on work/installation scope
role_scope: qualified and unqualified persons covered by Subpart S electrical safety-related work practices
notes: Defines covered work and distinguishes qualified/unqualified-person work-practice coverage. Does not by itself establish entertainment-industry job titles or local licensing rules.

title: 29 CFR 1910.332 — Training
jurisdiction_scope: US federal general industry where Subpart S applies
role_scope: employees exposed to electrical hazards; qualified and unqualified persons
notes: Exact source for job-assignment-specific electrical safety training and additional qualified-person training. It does not make an online Crew Blueprint course equivalent to qualified-person status.

title: 29 CFR 1910.333 — Selection and use of work practices
jurisdiction_scope: US federal general industry where Subpart S applies
role_scope: workers on or near exposed energized or deenergized electrical parts
notes: Exact authority source for deenergization/work-practice boundaries and the restriction of work on non-deenergized circuit parts/equipment to qualified persons. Crew Blueprint must not convert this into live-work instruction.

title: 29 CFR 1910.335 — Safeguards for personnel protection
jurisdiction_scope: US federal general industry where Subpart S applies
notes: Supports the need for appropriate protective measures and restricted access around exposed electrical hazards; not a substitute for task-specific qualified-person training.

title: 29 CFR 1910.399 — Definitions applicable to Subpart S
jurisdiction_scope: US federal general industry Subpart S
role_scope: electrical work covered by Subpart S
notes: Defines qualified person as one with training plus demonstrated skills/knowledge for the equipment/installations and hazards involved; qualification can be equipment/task specific.

title: 29 CFR 1910.305 — Wiring methods, components, and equipment for general use
jurisdiction_scope: US federal general industry; application depends on installation and work context
role_scope: electrical installations including temporary wiring where covered
notes: Exact federal temporary-wiring provisions where applicable. Do not generalize this section into a complete entertainment-power design standard or local code adoption rule.

title: Scope of Work for Entertainment Electrician and Portable Power Distribution Technician
jurisdiction_scope: ETCP certification scope; not statutory licensure by itself
role_scope: Entertainment Electrician and Portable Power Distribution Technician
notes: Credential-scope page. Direct source for the distinction between the broader Entertainment Electrician scope and the narrower PPDT power-distribution scope.

title: Entertainment Electrician — Get Certified
notes: Credential-eligibility page. Shows experience/training/licensure/education-based eligibility and current point requirements; certification eligibility is not the same as employer/site authorization or local licensure.

title: Portable Power Distribution Technician — Get Certified
notes: Credential-eligibility page. Shows experience-focused eligibility and that PPDT targets experienced portable-power-distribution workers; not an entry-level online-course credential.

title: Examination Content — Entertainment Electrician
notes: ETCP states the examination content derives from subject-matter-expert job analysis and practitioner input. Useful for competency-scope mapping, not a site authorization rule.

title: Examination Content — Portable Power Distribution Technician
notes: Supports portable-power competency-domain scope based on job analysis; does not authorize a specific worker on a specific site.

title: NFPA 70E — Standard for Electrical Safety in the Workplace, 2024 Edition
jurisdiction_scope: voluntary consensus standard unless adopted/required by employer, contract, venue, or AHJ; frequently referenced in OSHA enforcement guidance for electrical safety-related work practices
role_scope: qualified and unqualified persons working on or near exposed energized electrical conductors or circuit parts
notes: Consensus-standard cross-source for the qualified/unqualified person boundary already established in law by 29 CFR 1910.331-1910.335 and 1910.399 (S-OSHA-1910-331-CURRENT through S-OSHA-1910-399-CURRENT). Defines Restricted Approach Boundary (only qualified persons may cross) and Arc Flash Boundary (minimum safe distance without PPE) — supports an Electrics Course 1 boundary statement that an assigned support role recognizes and stays outside these boundaries rather than performs diagnostic or energized work. Free to read via NFPA's public-access portal; not a substitute for the controlling OSHA regulation text where the two differ.
